name: ridehail-driver-pay-optimization
description: Driver pay optimization for a ride-hailing marketplace on 360M real NYC TLC trips: PySpark + DuckDB pipeline, demand forecast, congestion-fee causal study, pay-to-accept model (DML, IV, Bayesian), constrained pay optimizer tested in a dispatch simulation, switchback test design, FastAPI + Docker, Streamlit demo.

paragraphs: What should a ride-hailing platform offer a driver for a trip? Pay too little and riders wait, cancel and drivers stop driving; pay too much and the margin disappears. This project answers that end to end on 360 million real New York City trips (January 2024 – June 2025): a PySpark pipeline, marketplace-health analytics in SQL, a demand forecast, a classifier, a causal study of a real policy change, a causal model of how drivers respond to pay, a constrained pay optimizer tested in a dispatch simulation, a quote API in Docker with CI/CD, and a switchback test to roll it out.

Scenario: the TLC records are treated as the history of one platform. Trips, pay, fares and waits are real; driver accept/decline decisions are simulated on top of them with a planted truth (the public data doesn't record them), which is what lets the causal methods be checked. Details below.
